name: Beth Patel

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and an experienced developer on travel-expense software for a tech company, with a bachelor’s degree. I know the claims system well, though I still ask finance staff about unusual cases. Jo works as a paramedic; with two school-age children and a mortgage, we are comfortable but still save rather than take on a car payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say our travel-expense software still needs a person to ask why a receipt was charged twice. I use AI now and then to draft a test, but I compare it with the actual claim before shipping.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a bachelor’s degree and a well-paid mid-level role, with about nine months of basic expenses saved. My partner Jo is a paramedic, and with two children and a mortgage we are comfortable while both wages continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep maintaining the reimbursement checks and ask finance support for the most common rejected receipt each month. We would keep putting 300 into savings monthly if both wages hold, rather than replace the car that still runs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel calm. A small AI shortcut does not change the bills we can already meet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which rejected receipt annoyed you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hotel charged a traveller twice for one night, but our screen marked both charges valid. I followed the two payment times until the finance team could reverse one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep saving with nine months banked?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A car repair and a school expense can arrive together. I would rather have cash than a newer car with a monthly payment.

say: I tell colleagues **double charges** still need a person checking the claim.
I compare occasional **AI tests** with actual receipts before release.
think: I have **nine months saved** and higher-than-usual developer pay.
I see **two steady wages** covering our mortgage and children now.
do: **Keep maintaining** expense checks and review one common rejected receipt monthly.
**Save 300 monthly** if both wages continue; keep the working car.
feel: **Calm** about work and the household budget.
S0.quote: I would rather have cash than a newer car with a monthly payment.
fieldNote: Her **receipt checks** connect software quality to a traveller’s real reimbursement.
A strong **nine-month cushion** and two wages support calm in this mild world, while she keeps saving for car and school costs.

steps.text: Keep maintaining expense checks and review rejected receipts with finance support
Save 300 monthly while both household wages continue
Keep the working car instead of taking a new car payment

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI taking checking, booking and coding is going to reach travel claims early, and we need to show which human signs a rejected claim. I would ask management for the staffing plan before calling faster processing a win.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the simple expense checks on my desk to disappear, leaving fewer people to review disputes. My hours could shrink even if the company’s clients stay. A cushion is not the same as a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d learn a new AI check for duplicate hotel charges using old receipts with names removed and compare its result with our recorded reversals. In the first year I’d ask the manager for a written list of roles and look at paid finance-support openings if my developer hours fall, accepting only pay that covers our mortgage and basic bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious about my own hours, though interested in testing the tool. A correct total matters more than a faster screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you know the AI check is sound?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d run it on the double-night hotel charge and five other old disputes. If it waves both charges through, I would not call it a saving.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a finance support role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if there is a paid vacancy and the wage covers the household bills. I know dispute work may also be automated later, so I would treat it as a current option, not a shelter forever.

say: I want **human sign-off** named for rejected travel claims.
I want a **staffing plan** before faster processing is called a win.
think: I expect **simple expense checks** to disappear from my desk.
I fear **my hours** could shrink even if clients stay.
do: **Learn AI duplicate-charge checks** on anonymized old receipts this month.
**Request roles list** and seek paid finance-support openings if hours fall.
**Accept support work** only if pay covers mortgage and basic bills.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, while interested in a testable tool.
S1.quote: A cushion is not the same as a wage.
fieldNote: She expects **routine checking** to shrink even with healthy company demand.
The **finance-support move** is conditional on a paid vacancy and bill-covering income; she does not assume disputes remain safe later.

steps.text: Learn AI duplicate-charge checks from anonymized hotel disputes
Seek paid finance-support openings if developer hours fall
Accept only support pay covering mortgage and basic bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could do nearly all our expense code and claim checking, for less. Robots for hands-on emergency care may arrive around 2031, so Jo’s paramedic work faces a later physical change than my screen job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my developer job could end even though I am experienced. Nine months saved and Jo’s wage would buy time, but I do not know whether many other software firms would be hiring then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d stop plans for a new car now and ask the company for a written date if developer roles end. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I lose my job, I’d apply for paid finance dispute work only where vacancies exist and pay covers our bills; I would use savings for mortgage payments during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed but not helpless. I can pay the mortgage for a while, yet I cannot put a new salary on the calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Jo cover everything?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the paramedic wage covers a lot but not the whole household for long. I would not ask Jo to take extra emergency shifts to make up for a company’s decision.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say the car can wait and we still have a place to live. I would tell them about a new job only when there is a real offer.

say: I say **thinking AGI by 2028** reaches expense code and claim checks.
I know **emergency-care robots around 2031** come later than my desk-work shock.
think: I expect my **developer job** could end despite experience.
I know **nine months saved** and Jo’s wage buy time, not a new salary.
do: **Stop planning car purchase** and request a written job date now.
**Apply for dispute work** only if displaced after 2028 and openings cover bills.
**Use savings for mortgage** while searching after a layoff.
feel: **Alarmed**, although savings and Jo’s wage buy some time.
S2.quote: I cannot put a new salary on the calendar.
fieldNote: She treats the **2028 thinking date** as the threat to her code, ahead of Jo’s physical work.
The **car decision** keeps cash available for the mortgage during a job search.

steps.text: Keep the current car instead of taking a new car payment
Apply for paid finance-dispute vacancies if displaced after 2028 and wages cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years before full AGI in 2031 gives companies time to decide who answers a traveller when a refund is wrong. Robots for hands-on emergency work may come around 2034, but my coding reaches AGI first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might learn more about claim disputes while I still have pay. Jo’s work and our cushion help, but I would not treat a finance job as safe from thinking AI in 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the claims lead for two anonymized hotel disputes each month to decide on paid time, if my manager approves. We would pay 200 extra toward mortgage principal monthly if both wages continue; after 2031 I’d seek paid finance-support roles only if my developer job ends and vacancies still cover our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious but able to practise. Five years gives me room to find out whether I actually like the complaint side of work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you put in the decision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The receipt dates, the duplicate charge and who authorised the reversal. I would ask the claims lead to tell me where my reasoning missed a step.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your manager refuses?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep the coding job and ask for old public examples. I would not count an unapproved exercise as training or give up paid hours.

say: I want a **named answerer** for wrong refunds before AGI reaches code in 2031.
I know **care robots around 2034** may later affect Jo’s hands-on work.
think: I could learn **claim disputes** while keeping my wage.
I know **finance support** may also be automated by 2031.
do: **Decide two anonymized disputes** monthly only with manager-approved paid time.
**Pay 200 extra** on the mortgage if both wages continue.
**Seek paid finance support** only if displaced after 2031 and vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Anxious but able** to test a real complaint skill.
S3.quote: I would not count an unapproved exercise as training or give up paid hours.
fieldNote: Her **claim decisions** are actual practice, conditional on paid manager approval.
Mortgage prepayment remains **independent** of that approval and depends on both wages continuing through the five-year preparation period.

steps.text: Decide two anonymized hotel disputes monthly only with manager-approved paid time
Pay 200 extra monthly toward mortgage principal if both wages hold
Seek paid finance-support vacancies only if displaced after 2031 and pay covers bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade before full AGI in 2036 gives families time to pay down debt and companies time to make claim rules clear. Robots for emergency hands-on work may follow around 2039, after our code changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children would be older, but I cannot budget for their wages. If both our jobs last, we could pay off a chunk of the mortgage and build a year of basic bills, though code and disputes may both change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep maintaining the travel-expense app and record one disputed receipt each month without traveller names, including how it was resolved. We would save 250 monthly if both wages hold; if my developer role ends after 2036, I’d seek paid claims-audit work only where vacancies remain and pay covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel uneasy about 2036 but secure in the next few years. I like having time to make the household numbers better without betting on a permanent safe job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show a future employer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A page describing the mistake, the evidence and the corrected claim, with all personal details removed. I would rather demonstrate how I resolve a travel claim than promise I can learn it later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move for that work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if there is a written paid offer covering a new housing cost and the children’s school travel. Plenty of software firms are nearby, so we would try the local market before disrupting school.

say: I want **clear claim rules** before AGI reaches expense code in 2036.
I know **care robots around 2039** follow the software change.
think: I will not budget for **children’s future wages**.
I could build **a year of bills** if both jobs continue.
do: **Keep maintaining claims** and record resolved receipts without names.
**Save 250 monthly** if both household wages hold.
**Try local firms first**; seek bill-covering claims work after 2036 displacement, moving only for written pay covering housing and school travel.
feel: **Uneasy about 2036**, secure in the next few years.
S4.quote: I would rather demonstrate how I resolve a travel claim than promise I can learn it later.
fieldNote: Her **receipt record** shows concrete evidence of judgment without exposing travellers.
She would move only for **written pay** covering new housing and school travel, after trying local firms first.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my developer wage could end before a paid alternative is clear. A written job date, real finance-dispute openings that cover our bills and time to use our nine-month cushion carefully would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who has to take the extra shifts if I lose work. I would not make Jo carry a company’s decision by working more emergency nights. I would not make my partner Jo work extra emergency nights to cover my lost developer wage.

headlineQuote: I would not make my partner Jo work extra emergency nights to cover my lost developer wage.
portrait: Beth is a **43-year-old mid-level developer** with a bachelor’s degree, higher pay and nine months of expenses saved.
She and Jo cover **two children** and a mortgage, with Jo working as a paramedic.
She uses AI **occasionally after testing** it against real travel receipts.
Her **2028 risk** is losing a coding wage before a paid claims role exists, while care robots arrive later.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her developer wage despite nine months saved.
whatWouldHelp: A **written job date**, bill-covering finance vacancies and time to use the cushion carefully would help.
